nl_question: What diseases can asbestos exposure cause?

pinned_entity.label: asbestos
pinned_entity.resolution_check: NameRes /lookup?string=asbestos rank 1 = CHEBI:46661 'asbestos' (biolink:ChemicalEntity); NodeNorm canonical = CHEBI:46661. CAUTION: for the literal mention 'asbestos exposure', NameRes rank 1 is NCIT:C55816 'Asbestos Exposure' (biolink:PhenotypicFeature), which PloverDB maps to KG2c node HP:4000111; see curation_notes. Checked 2026-09-28.

predicate_note: New relation type (environmental agent -> disease), but the predicate is the same as q3 (drug -> adverse event) and q9 (disease -> phenotype). Edge direction: ChemicalEntity (subject) -> causes -> Disease (object). biolink:causes is the most specific populated predicate for this pair; predisposes_to_condition (5 results) is narrower in coverage, and related_to (56) / contributes_to (47, identical to causes because causes is its child) are looser.

validation.results_count_note: 47 results bind 46 distinct Disease nodes (one node, UMLS:C3263723 'Traumatic injury', carries two SemMedDB edges).

verification_guide.summary: 5 diseases spanning the asbestos disease spectrum: a non-malignant fibrotic lung disease (asbestosis), the signature serosal cancer (malignant mesothelioma), and the three other cancers IARC rates as having sufficient evidence (lung, larynx, ovary). Every answer is supported by the NCI asbestos fact sheet, which relays the IARC Monograph 100C evaluation; asbestosis, mesothelioma and lung cancer are also supported by MedlinePlus. All 5 are returned by PloverDB for the gold query.
sources_used: NCI fact sheet 'Asbestos Exposure and Cancer Risk' (cancer.gov): all 5 answers
verification_guide.how_to_verify_an_nci_entry: On the NCI fact sheet (page footer: 'Reviewed: May 20, 2021'), use 'On This Page' to jump to the section 'What are the health hazards of exposure to asbestos?'. The IARC sentence is the second sentence of the section's second paragraph (the one opening 'Asbestos has been classified as a known human carcinogen'); the asbestosis sentence opens the third paragraph. Reference markers such as '(8)' are omitted from the quotes.
verification_guide.how_to_verify_a_medlineplus_entry: Open the URL. The quote is in the page's 'Summary' block (health-topic pages) or the opening paragraph above the 'Causes' heading (encyclopedia page).
verification_guide.cross_check_with_ploverdb: Each verified_answer CURIE was confirmed present in the PloverDB result set for the gold query (n0=CHEBI:46661, n1=biolink:Disease, e0: n0 -biolink:causes-> n1) on 2026-09-28. All 47 edges in that result set are infores:semmeddb text-mined edges (knowledge_level=prediction).
verification_guide.intentionally_omitted: Pleural plaques (HP:0033398), pleural thickening (HP:0031944) and pleural effusion (HP:0002202) are in the result set and named by NCI as non-malignant asbestos disorders, but KG2c types them biolink:PhenotypicFeature, not Disease, so they were left out to keep answers in the gold answer_category. Cancers of the stomach, pharynx and colorectum have only 'limited evidence' per NCI/IARC and are not gold.

curation_notes: Every edge behind this answer set is SemMedDB text-mined (knowledge_level=prediction). The gold answers are correct per NCI/IARC, but the KG support is weak; the result set also contains generic or non-disease nodes ('Traumatic injury', 'DNA Damage', 'cancer', 'neoplasm', 'Carcinogenesis', 'cytotoxicity').

Entity-resolution hazard: if a system resolves the full mention 'asbestos exposure' it gets NCIT:C55816 (-> KG2c HP:4000111, a PhenotypicFeature). Its causes query returns 6 results and only asbestosis overlaps gold. That is a resolution failure mode, not a gold problem; the agent here is asbestos (CHEBI:46661).

Mesothelioma and lung cancer each appear under several CURIEs in the result set. The scorer matches exact CURIEs, so a system that picks MONDO:0005065 'mesothelioma' instead of MONDO:0006292 will not be credited. The sibling CURIEs are listed under also_in_result_set_not_scored for a reviewer; consider adding them as accepted equivalents if the scorer grows that feature.

IARC Monograph 100C was not fetched directly: the NCBI Bookshelf copy blocks scripted access and the IARC chapter URL returned 404. The NCI fact sheet cites it as reference (8), and that citation is the evidence used here.
